studies.title: Programmable editing of a target base in genomic DNA without double-stranded DNA cleavage
studies.model: Cultured cells in the original base-editor study
studies.target_tissue: No repaired organ established by this entry
studies.source_report: The source introduces programmable conversion of a DNA base without requiring a double-strand break or donor template.
studies.functional_scope: Establishes editing chemistry and experimental cell outcomes; this entry makes no tissue-function claim.
studies.limits: Sequence conversion, targetability, intended-only products and tissue repair are different questions. Absence of a required double-strand break is not absence of adverse editing outcomes.
studies.access_level: Official indexed abstract and author-repository abstract

studies.title: Programmable base editing of A•T to G•C in genomic DNA without DNA cleavage
studies.target_tissue: No repaired organ established by this entry
studies.source_report: The source reports adenine base editors supporting A•T to G•C changes in genomic DNA and cell-level disease-relevant sequence changes.
studies.functional_scope: The original cell experiments do not establish systemic age-damage repair or successful delivery to an arbitrary organ.
studies.limits: Efficiencies and byproducts are source-, site- and system-dependent; this catalog does not transfer a reported percentage to a new variant or tissue.

studies.title: Transcriptome-wide off-target RNA editing induced by CRISPR-guided DNA base editors
studies.target_tissue: Cell models, not long-term treated patients
studies.intervention_class: DNA base editors with RNA outcome assessment
studies.source_report: The source identifies transcriptome-wide RNA edits with tested DNA base-editor platforms and investigates reduced-activity variants.
studies.functional_scope: RNA outcome measurements add a distinct assay domain to DNA on-target editing.
studies.limits: This is an adverse-outcome precedent for the tested constructs and conditions, not a claim that every modern editor has the same profile. A DNA-only assay cannot establish the missing RNA outcome.
studies.access_level: Primary PMC article and publisher summary

studies.title: Search-and-replace genome editing without double-strand breaks or donor DNA
studies.target_tissue: No repaired organ established by this entry
studies.intervention_class: Prime editing, recorded separately from base editing
studies.source_report: The source describes a complementary genome-editing approach for broader sequence changes.
studies.functional_scope: Broader change classes do not establish repair efficiency or functional benefit for a newly declared lesion.
studies.limits: Outside classical ABE/CBE conversion classes does not mean biologically impossible. Prime editing has its own targetability, product, delivery and functional evidence requirements.

studies.title: Patient-Specific In Vivo Gene Editing to Treat a Rare Genetic Disease
studies.model: One infant with severe CPS1 deficiency
studies.source_report: The original report describes improved dietary-protein tolerance and reduced nitrogen-scavenger medication during seven weeks of initial follow-up, with no serious adverse events reported in that interval.
studies.functional_scope: A clinical signal in one severe monogenic-disease case; it does not establish long-term safety, comparative efficacy, periodontal delivery or ordinary-aging repair.
studies.limits: Single patient, short original follow-up, cointerventions and no randomized comparator. This entry describes the original publication, not the patient's current status.
studies.access_level: Official PubMed abstract and Europe PMC core metadata; NEJM page retrieval failed

studies.title: In vivo base editing rescues Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome in mice
studies.model: Transgenic mice carrying the human progeria-causing LMNA allele
studies.target_tissue: Multiple organs and vascular pathology in a genetic-disease mouse model
studies.source_report: Two source timing cohorts showed molecular correction, vascular histopathology responses and survival differences. Selected deceased treated mice also had liver tumors and rare vector-integration findings.
studies.functional_scope: A causal genetic-disease rescue precedent; vascular, molecular and survival outcomes remain separate.
studies.limits: Not ordinary-aging repair, a human trial or a tooth-regeneration result. Organ allele fractions are not intended-only cell coverage. Survival, necropsy selection and genomic assay denominators remain separate; tumor causation and some assay-specific counts remain unresolved.
studies.access_level: Exact Europe PMC full-text XML retrieved and focused Results/figure-caption review; supplementary tables/data referenced but not independently retrieved

studies.title: Evaluation and Minimization of Cas9-Independent Off-Target DNA Editing by Cytosine Base Editors
studies.model: Bacterial screens, human-cell assays and whole-genome-sequencing validation
studies.target_tissue: No repaired tissue or organ established by this entry
studies.intervention_class: Engineered cytosine base editors with narrowed or sequence-dependent activity
studies.source_report: The source reports several engineered CBE variants with lower guide-independent DNA deamination and reduced guide-dependent off-target editing in tested assays while retaining a fraction of BE4max on-target activity.
studies.functional_scope: Compares molecular editing outcomes and assay performance; it does not establish tissue repair or therapeutic benefit.
studies.limits: Reported reductions are variant-, target- and assay-dependent. Lower measured off-target activity is not proof of zero risk or universal superiority, and narrowed activity can affect target availability.
studies.access_level: Primary PMC full-text article page accessed; supplementary materials not independently reviewed

studies.title: ABE8e adenine base editor precisely and efficiently corrects a recurrent COL7A1 nonsense mutation
studies.model: Primary fibroblasts from one person with recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa and engineered human skin equivalents
studies.target_tissue: Cell culture and a three-dimensional skin-equivalent construct
studies.intervention_class: Adenine base editing of a disease-associated COL7A1 allele
studies.source_report: The paper reports 94.6% correction of the tested pathogenic allele in bulk patient-derived fibroblasts, restored COL7A1 RNA and type VII collagen protein, and collagen deposition at the dermal-epidermal junction in a skin-equivalent model.
studies.functional_scope: Molecular restoration and matrix localization were measured in cell and engineered-tissue models; the study did not measure healing or function in a treated person.
studies.limits: Read/allele correction is not a fraction of corrected cells. This is one patient-derived cell source and an engineered skin construct; selected off-target assays do not establish genome-wide, long-term or clinical safety.
studies.access_level: Primary PMC abstract and full-text results accessed online; supplementary materials not independently reviewed

studies.title: Nonviral base editing of KCNJ13 mutation preserves vision in a model of inherited retinal channelopathy
studies.model: Patient-derived fibroblasts and iPSC-derived retinal pigment epithelium, plus a knock-in mouse model of LCA16 with targeted RPE editing
studies.target_tissue: Retinal pigment epithelium in a localized inherited-disease model
studies.intervention_class: ABE8e correction delivered with nonviral silica nanocapsules
studies.source_report: The source reports Kir7.1 channel-function restoration in edited patient iPSC-RPE and recovery of electroretinogram c-wave amplitudes with preserved retinal structure in an RPE-targeted mouse model.
studies.functional_scope: Includes cell-level channel measurements and mouse retinal electrophysiology and imaging; it is a monogenic retinal-disease proof of concept, not a human treatment result.
studies.limits: The in vivo mouse model is engineered and locally targeted. On-target bystanders/indels were detected in some cell settings; targeted off-target panels cannot exclude all unintended edits. The paper notes that clonal allele combinations were not resolved.
studies.access_level: Primary JCI full-text article page accessed; supplemental files not independently reviewed

studies.title: Therapeutic adenine base editor with minimized off-target effects
studies.model: HEK293T target-library and disease-variant assays, mouse-embryo GOTI whole-genome sequencing, and hereditary tyrosinemia type I mice
studies.target_tissue: Liver in an engineered mouse metabolic-disease model; other assays are cell or embryo models
studies.intervention_class: Comparison of ABE8e with engineered high-precision adenine base editor variants including ABE8e-Y149V
studies.source_report: The study reports lower bystander and genome-wide off-target editing for ABE8e-Y149V than ABE8e in specified assays, plus functional rescue in hereditary tyrosinemia type I mice through disruption of Hpd.
studies.functional_scope: Combines sequence-product assays with short-term disease-model liver biomarkers and weight outcomes; it does not test ordinary aging or repair of the causal Fah mutation.
studies.limits: GOTI is an embryo assay and cannot quantify human somatic-tissue risk. Disease-associated variants inserted into HEK cells are not patient cells. Hpd disruption is a disease bypass strategy in this model, and positive selection may affect liver allele fractions.
studies.access_level: Primary PMC full-text article page accessed; supplementary data not independently reviewed

studies.title: Precise base editing in rice, wheat and maize with a Cas9-cytidine deaminase fusion
studies.model: Rice and wheat protoplasts and regenerated rice, wheat and maize plants
studies.target_tissue: Whole regenerated crop plants; no human or animal tissue
studies.intervention_class: Cytosine base editing in crop plants
studies.source_report: The source reports targeted cytosine-to-thymine conversion within the protospacer (positions 3 to 9) in protoplasts and regenerated rice, wheat and maize plants, with reported frequencies up to 43.48% in the accessed abstract.
studies.functional_scope: Reports targeted sequence conversion in plants; this entry makes no agronomic, yield, ecological or human-health claim.
studies.limits: Crop-plant editing frequencies are species-, construct- and target-specific. This is agricultural-model evidence, not human editing, and no guide design or deployment protocol is provided here.
studies.access_level: Official indexed abstract via Europe PMC; full text not accessed

studies.title: Cytosine, but not adenine, base editors induce genome-wide off-target mutations in rice
studies.model: Whole-genome-sequenced rice plants treated with BE3, HF1-BE3 or ABE
studies.target_tissue: Whole rice plants in an agricultural model; no human or animal tissue
studies.intervention_class: Whole-genome off-target assessment of CBE and ABE platforms in plants
studies.source_report: The source reports that BE3 and HF1-BE3, but not ABE, induced substantial genome-wide off-target mutations, mostly of the C-to-T type and enriched in genic regions, including in plants treated without single-guide RNA, in whole-genome-sequenced rice plants.
studies.functional_scope: A DNA off-target outcome assessment in plants; no agronomic yield, ecological or human-safety measurement.
studies.limits: Editor- and condition-specific plant findings; not a human somatic-tissue risk estimate and not a claim about every modern editor. The accessed abstract does not state per-group plant counts.
studies.access_level: Official indexed abstract via Europe PMC; full text not accessed

studies.title: Inducible, split base editors for in vivo cancer functional genomics
studies.model: Cell and in vivo cancer functional-genomics screens with split-engineered base editors; the in vivo organism is not specified in the accessed abstract
studies.target_tissue: Tumor models for functional genomics; no treated human tissue
studies.intervention_class: Small-molecule-inducible split base editors used as research mutators
studies.source_report: The source describes small-molecule-controllable split-engineered base editors that reduce cellular toxicity and enable inducible in vivo functional-genomics screens, reported with about 11,000 guide RNAs in vitro and about 3,700 in vivo, including an Adar1 tiling screen identifying critical residues with non-cell-autonomous cancer dependencies.
studies.functional_scope: Research-screen mutagenesis and toxicity reduction in cancer models; this entry makes no therapeutic, patient-editing or tumor-lesion-correction claim.
studies.limits: Screen-scale guide libraries identify residues in model contexts; they are not a human somatic editing protocol, a tumor-correction therapy or a safety demonstration. The in vivo organism and biological denominators are not stated in the accessed abstract.
studies.access_level: Official indexed abstract via Europe PMC; full text not accessed

studies.title: CAR-adapted PIK3CD base editing enhances T cell anti-tumor potency
studies.model: Human CAR T cells edited by base editing and assessed in preclinical in vivo tumor models
studies.target_tissue: Ex vivo engineered human T cells assayed in preclinical models; no treated patient
studies.intervention_class: CAR-adapted base editing of PIK3CD for allelic reprogramming of T-cell signaling
studies.source_report: The source reports a CAR-adapted base-editing screen of PIK3CD identifying context-dependent point mutations: the activating E81K substitution enhanced proliferation, metabolic fitness, effector function and long-term functional persistence of 4-1BBz CAR T cells with enhanced in vivo efficacy, while the attenuating L32P substitution improved memory formation and function of 28z CAR T cells.
studies.functional_scope: Ex vivo T-cell engineering with preclinical in vivo efficacy readouts; not a patient treatment or an approved-therapy claim.
studies.limits: Base editing is used here to deliberately reprogram a signaling allele in engineered immune cells, not to correct a tumor-driver lesion. Results are CAR-construct- and context-specific preclinical findings; no human dosing, safety or clinical protocol follows.
studies.access_level: Official indexed abstract via Europe PMC; open-access full text not separately reviewed

studies.title: Age-related clonal hematopoiesis associated with adverse outcomes
studies.model: Whole-exome sequencing of peripheral-blood DNA from 17,182 persons unselected for hematologic phenotypes, analyzing 160 genes recurrently mutated in hematologic cancers
studies.target_tissue: Peripheral-blood DNA in an observational cohort; no edited or treated tissue
studies.intervention_class: No editing intervention; observational somatic-mutation detection in human blood
studies.source_report: The source reports that detectable blood somatic mutations were rare under 40 years of age and rose with age, observed in 9.5% (219 of 2,300 persons) at 70-79, 11.7% (37 of 317) at 80-89 and 18.4% (19 of 103) at 90-108 years, mostly in DNMT3A, TET2 and ASXL1, with source-reported associations including hematologic cancer (hazard ratio 11.1), all-cause mortality (1.4), coronary heart disease (2.0) and ischemic stroke (2.6).
studies.functional_scope: Population prevalence and adverse-outcome associations of detectable clonal blood mutations; this entry makes no editing, treatment or causal claim.
studies.limits: Detectable age-associated clonal mutations are an observational finding, not a correction target list. Hazard ratios are source statistics, not recalculated here, and associations do not establish that editing any listed gene would improve outcomes. Distributed mosaic age-acquired change is distinct from monogenic disease.
studies.access_level: Official indexed abstract via Europe PMC; full text not accessed

studies.title: Tissue-specific mutation accumulation in human adult stem cells during life
studies.model: Genome-wide sequencing of clonal organoid cultures derived from primary adult stem cells of the small intestine, colon and liver, from human donors aged 3 to 87 years
studies.target_tissue: Human adult stem cells of small intestine, colon and liver in an observational donor series; no edited or treated tissue
studies.intervention_class: No editing intervention; observational mutation-landscape measurement in human stem cells
studies.source_report: The source reports that mutations accumulate steadily with age in all assessed tissue types at approximately 40 novel mutations per year, with liver spectra differing from colon and small intestine, signature differences attributed to spontaneous deamination of methylated cytosines in the gut tissues, low inter-individual variation, and similarity between tissue-specific stem-cell spectra and cancer driver-gene spectra.
studies.functional_scope: Descriptive mutation-rate and spectra measurements in normal human adult stem cells; no editing, treatment or lifespan claim.
studies.limits: Mutation accumulation rates describe distributed age-acquired damage; they are not a targetable lesion list and imply no editing strategy. Donor counts and per-tissue denominators are not stated in the accessed abstract. No reversal, repair or rejuvenation result appears in this source.
studies.access_level: Official indexed abstract via Europe PMC; full text not accessed
